ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, P is marked at the center of the circle, and radii are drawn from P to B, Y, C, A, and X on the circle. In the figure X, P, and Y are on the same straight line, so XY is a diameter; B, P, and A are also on the same straight line, so BA is a diameter. The central angle ∠BPY is marked as 3x°, ∠YPC is marked as (3x − 3)°, and ∠CPA is marked as (2x + 15)°. What the problem asks for is the measure of arc YC. Reasoning: The measure of arc YC is equal to the corresponding central angle ∠YPC, so m arc YC = 3x − 3. Because BA and XY are two straight lines passing through P, ∠APX and ∠BPY are vertical angles, so ∠APX = 3x°. Along the semicircle from Y to X, passing through C and A, the sum of the central angles is 180°, therefore (3x − 3) + (2x + 15) + 3x = 180. Combining gives 8x + 12 = 180, so 8x = 168, x = 21. Substituting into m arc YC = 3x − 3 gives 3(21) − 3 = 60.
